how: Beijing's highest point, Mount Ling (Dongling, 2,303 m), lies in Mentougou about 120 km west of downtown (roughly 2.5 hours by road); no alpine mountaineering terrain exists within 30 km.
No desert dunes lie near Beijing; the nearest dune fields are in the Kubuqi Desert in Inner Mongolia, several hundred kilometres west (a flight plus road transfer).
Only show caves are accessible: Shihuadong (Stone Flower Cave) and Yinhu Cave in Fangshan district, about 40 km southwest of the centre, with guided tourist routes rather than free caving.
A bungee jumping tower stands inside Chaoyang Park (mapped in OpenStreetMap and listed on Wikivoyage); operating status and current prices are not confirmed.

The Beijing Shooting Range Clay Target Field in Shijingshan hosted the 2008 Olympic shotgun events; public or recreational clay sessions are not confirmed and Chinese firearm rules restrict casual shooting.

how: Xiaotangshan in Changping, about 30 km north of the centre, has a 1,500-year history of geothermal hot-spring bathing and is home to hot-spring bathing resorts.
